name: policy-composition-with-not
description: Demonstrates boolean composition (AND/OR/NOT) over multiple claim-graph resolvers, including negation of a delegated sub-policy. Copy-pasteable example showing how to express 'the issuer must hold A AND B, must NOT have been revoked, and the subject must either have passed KYC OR be on a trusted allow-list'.

trace: and[1] -> and[1.0] resolve good-standing active: PASS
and[1] -> and[1.1] resolve revocation-list does NOT include issuer: PASS
and[1] -> and[1.2] not( delegated policy flagged sanctioned ): PASS (sanctioned=false)
and[2] -> or[2.0] resolve kyc level=enhanced: PASS (short-circuits or)
ROOT: AND of all PASS => allow=true

notes: Boolean operators 'and', 'or', 'not' are commutative except 'not' which wraps exactly one child.
Short-circuit evaluation: 'or' stops on first PASS; 'and' stops on first FAIL; 'not' always evaluates its child then inverts.

Each 'resolve' node binds to a named resolver (attestation-resolver, revocation-resolver, allowlist-resolver, delegated-policy-resolver) — see patterns/claim-graph-resolver/src/cache.ts for the resolver interface.
expect_not_includes is the array-negation companion to expect_includes; useful for revocation and denylist checks.

Recursion safety: the 'not' node pointing at a delegated policy is bounded by the cycle-detector (see patterns/claim-graph-resolver/src/cycle-detector.ts); policies that loop through negation are rejected at load time.

Failure-mode example: if the issuer is in the revocation list, and[1.1] fails, the root AND fails fast and allow=false; the trace records the first FAIL only by default — set trace_mode='all' to capture every node evaluation.
